Mockup · AEON-1196 Agents page consolidation · round 6 Person Layout Widths320 px Width Mode

AEON-1196 · Agents page · round 7 (for approval)

TL;DR: one floating bar (the app header), then the page head, then the capacity row, then the Sessions card.

  • Sessions card: its head carries the list’s own tools and sticks inside the card.
  • Split: one continuous split. The divider is the truth: the list’s own width decides its form, and past 380 px of details it closes.
  • Layout button: only jumps the divider to presets (Focus · Overview · List only). It sits at the work area’s top-right corner and never moves.
  • Details: always start at their top, full height under the header, with the session actions in their head.
  • Dial: lighter; each unit is bound by proximity, with no pills.
  • Avatar: carries only the state badge.

Phone and dark are covered for every state.

1 · Decisions

  1. One floating bar. Only the app header floats over the page. The Sessions card head sticks inside its card, at the card’s width, under the header, so it reads as part of the list. The capacity row scrolls with the page. Sticking adds a hairline shadow only: zero shift.
  2. List tools live on the list. The header searches everything; “Search sessions” only filters this list.
    • The card head reads: Sessions 39 · Collapse/Expand all · Search sessions (F or /) · Filter · Display … the layout button.
    • The pills (the state filter from the counts included) and the column heads sit under it and stick with it.
    • Grouping is unchanged: by project, the lead row heading its group. Group by lead, harness, state, computer or none stays available in Display.
  3. The divider is the truth; the button is only a preset. One continuous split; the handle position (the list’s width) is remembered per person.
    • The list’s own width decides its form: compact rows under 560 px, the full table from 560 px. Crossing 560 changes only the rows’ form.
    • Dragging is live. Let go with less than 380 px of details and they close (List only); the list never goes under 280 px, and there is no details-only state.
    • The button jumps the handle: Focus (list 320 px) → Overview (details 480 px) → List only. Its icon shows the state the handle is nearest to, its tooltip names the next, and S does the same.
    • Opening a session from List only uses the remembered handle (the Overview preset the first time). Esc or × returns to List only.
    • Presets animate in 240 ms, or instantly with reduced motion.
    • The split exists only when both presets fit: a 560 px table, 16 px and 480 px of details, i.e. a 1056 px work area (about an 1100 px window). Narrower windows and phones open a session as a sheet over the list, and the button hides.
  4. The button stays put, always top right. It lives in one sticky dock at the work area’s top-right corner and is never re-parented.
    • In List only it is the right end of the Sessions head; in a split it is the right end of the details head, after ⋯ and ×.
    • Both heads keep room for it. Its box is identical in all three states and at every scroll position once the work area has reached the header.
    • × stays: it closes in one step from any split, while the button’s next step from Focus is Overview.
  5. Details always start at the top. In a split both columns are viewport-high panes under the app header, each with its own scroll.
    • Reaching the split scrolls the page so the work area starts right under the header.
    • Picking any session shows its details from their top. The picked row stays where it was under the pointer: the list pane scrolls, the page does not.
    • The details’ own scroll resets when the selection changes.
  6. Session actions at the top. Interrupt · Pause (Resume when paused; Pause… opens LeadPauseSheet for a lead) · Stop… (danger ghost) sit in the panel head, next to ⋯, on every tab, for leads and workers.
    • Narrow details (Overview, the phone sheet) show them as icons, with the words in tooltips and aria.
    • On the phone they take their own line under the name. Every target is 44 px on touch.
    • A stopped lead’s Start a lead moves into Right now.
  7. A lighter dial. The units (the total and each harness) have no outline and no fill; they are bound by proximity.
    • Icon and number are 4 px apart; units are 16 px apart with a faint 16 px hairline between them.
    • At the limit shows a gold ‖ after the number, with no fill.
    • When the row has room (900 px or more, as at 1440), − / + sit inline, muted, in reserved room and appear on hover or focus.
    • When the row is tight, they appear on a light floating plate over the neighbours (shadow only, no outline) that never pushes anything.
    • On touch, a tap opens the plate. The unfolded dial’s harness list drops its selection ring for a faint tint.
  8. Header order (AEON-1139): Projects · Agents · Business · Decision Desk. The Desk is a split button, last, on desktop and phone: the name goes to the Desk, and the ▾ opens the preview (the old Desk chip’s dropdown, unchanged).
  9. The avatar carries the state badge only. It is the live system (Robot 5 with its AgentStateMark; the STATE_LABEL is the tooltip and part of the aria-label), with no HarnessBadge overlay.
    • The wide table’s Execution column is the one home of the model (mark, “Opus 5.5 · xhigh”, the account).
    • Compact rows (the Focus sidebar and the phone), where Execution is hidden, open line 1 with a 12 px harness mark. Its tooltip and aria read e.g. “Opus 5.5 · xhigh · Claude Code · Claude Max”.
    • Panel heads name the model in their subtitle.
  10. Page head: Agents · the state counts (working · waiting · problems; throttled and paused only when there are any) · Wind down · More · New, with New last.
  11. A lead that waits for a person is waiting. Line 2 says what it asks, and it opens on Chat. The queue chip opens Lead at Next up: on line 1 in the wide table, and at the start of line 2 in compact rows, so a lead’s name never truncates first.
  12. One lead panel: Lead · Session · Chat. It opens on what needs you, then your default, then the tab you used last, and one line says why. Workers keep Overview · Chat.
  13. Folded groups are remembered per person. A folded lead sums up its workers on line 2 (“· 5 workers · 1 problem · 1 question”). Collapse all / Expand all is a muted ghost icon that writes the same preference.
  14. A state change is a state. Rows enter and leave only at the moments in 3.2; ended rows keep their end state for 10 minutes. Tooltips never cover their own open popover.
  15. Keys are plain keys only (3.5). F or / focuses the list search, and S cycles the layout. On /agents, “/” leaves the command palette: AppHeader’s pageOwnsSlash gains /agents.

3 · Spec

3.1 The split: handle ranges, presets and the space rule (the handle is the list’s width, a per-person preference)

Handle (list width)List formDetailsIcon shows
280–559 pxCompact rows (name and time; what it works on; the opener mark)The rest, full heightFocus
560 px to the work width − 16 − 380The full table (Time, Execution, Computer, Beat)The rest, at least 380 px, full heightOverview
Released with less than 380 px of detailsFull widthClosedList only
Under 280 pxNot possible: dragging left stops there. There is no details-only state.
Preset (button or S)SetsFrom there, nextEsc
FocusList 320 pxOverviewCloses the details → List only
OverviewDetails 480 px (list = the rest)List onlyCloses the details → List only
List onlyNo detailsFocusClears a count filter, if one is on

The space rule: the split exists when both presets fit: 560 + 16 + 480 = 1056 px of work area, about an 1100 px window. Narrower, or on a phone, a session opens as a sheet over the list, Esc or Back closes it, and the button hides. Opening from List only reopens at the remembered handle, clamped to the window.

3.2 When rows enter and leave (AEON-541; the UI rule for AEON-1195, whose data fix stays separate)

  • A state change is a state. The row stays; its badge, line 2 and time change, never its height.
  • Changes in structure are held while the pointer is over the list, focus is in a row, or a menu is open. That covers new sessions, rows going to Ended, and group changes.
    • The card head says “2 changes wait while you point here · Show now”.
    • The changes apply 1.5 s after the pointer leaves, on Show now, or when the page loads.
  • Where rows land: a new worker lands last under its lead, and a new lead at its project’s fixed place.
  • Ended rows: a done or ended row keeps its place and end state for 10 minutes, then moves to Ended at the next allowed moment.

3.3 Grouping

  • Group by Project (the default): projects in the sidebar’s fixed order. The lead row heads each group, with workers nested in start order.
  • A project with queued work and no lead is one slim line. “No project” and “Ended N” come at the end.
  • Folded groups are the person preference agents:layout.folded_projects. The split handle (the list’s width) is agents:layout.handle.

3.4 Deep links

  • /agents/:sessionId opens the session at the remembered handle (the Overview preset the first time), or as a sheet when the window is too narrow. A lead opens on what needs you, then your default, then the tab you used last.
  • ?tab=chat|lead|session forces a tab. ?tab=lead#next-up is the queue.
  • /agents?filter=… sets a count filter; ?q=, project=, harness=, computer= and group= carry the list tools.
  • ?run=<id> works as today. The layout and its widths are preferences, not URL state.

5 · Build notes: packages of 6–10 h

  1. P1 · Head, capacity row and the card head (9 h).
    • Head order; the capacity row with the lighter dial units (r6 change 5, r7 change 1) and the accounts chip with its three tiles (AEON-1176 P6).
    • The Sessions card head with ListToolbar’s search, Filter and Display, sticking inside the card (changes 1 and 2); the one control height.
    • Remove DecisionDeskPanel (AEON-1139).
    • D1 (AEON-1166) and P6’s inline pace edit stay in the dial’s own package and get checked against the units.
  2. P2 · Grouped tree (9 h). SessionList by project with lead rows, the no-lead line, the queue chip and the tree; DisplayPanel and FilterMenu for sessions, with the pills under the card head (change 2); folded-groups preference and Collapse all.
  3. P3 · State in the icon, compact rows and enter/leave (8 h).
    • The avatar with the state badge only; the Time column; compact rows with the 12 px opener.
    • The held-changes rule and the 10-minute end states. This is AEON-1195’s UI half.
  4. P4 · One lead panel (9 h). Lead · Session · Chat; opening on what needs you, the pinned default and last used; session actions in the head (change 4); the question card; the Next up deep link.
  5. P5 · The split, the fixed button and keys (10 h).
    • One continuous split, the divider as truth: the form at 560 px, the close past 380 px of details, the 280 px minimum, the handle as a per-person preference, and the space rule with its sheet (r7 change 2).
    • The preset button in its sticky top-right dock (r7 change 3).
    • Viewport-high panes, with the work area brought under the header and the details starting at their top (r7 change 4).
    • The animation, F, / and S, and pageOwnsSlash.
  6. P6 · Header Desk split button (6 h, its own package next to AEON-1139). The place order with the Desk last (change 6); the link plus chevron; the preview dropdown on every page; 44 px on the phone.

Every package: phone and dark in its acceptance, and check.mjs as its gate. The gate covers zero shift, no edge accents, SVG icons, 44 px targets, keys, avatar badges, English, and no sideways scroll at 390.
